'''Robert Michael Pittilo''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|MBE}} (7 October 1954 &ndash; 16 February 2010) was a British biologist and [[Principal (education)|Principal]] and [[Chancellor (education)#Vice-chancellor|vice-chancellor]] of the [[Robert Gordon University]], in [[Aberdeen]], [[Scotland]]. Pittilo worked in research and education for most of his adult life, holding a number of positions at universities throughout the United Kingdom, notably as Foundation Dean of the Faculty of Health and Social Care Sciences at [[Kingston University]] and [[St George's, University of London|St George's]], [[University of London]], and as Pro Vice-Chancellor of the [[University of Hertfordshire]].

==Early life==
Pittilo was born in Edinburgh.<ref name="RGU1">{{cite web|title=RGU:The Principal|url=https://www3.rgu.ac.uk/files/dmfile/NexusMarch2010.pdf|publisher=[[Robert Gordon University]]|accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref> He was educated at the [[independent school (UK)|independent]] [[Kelvinside Academy]] in [[Glasgow]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/obituaries/michael-pittilo-principal-and-vice-chancellor-of-robert-gordon-university-1-791212|title=Michael Pittilo, principal and vice-chancellor of Robert Gordon University|date=17 February 2010|accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref> and both the [[University of Strathclyde]] and [[University of East London]],<ref name="RGU1"/> where he studied biology, graduating in 1976.<ref name="RGU2">{{cite web|title=RGU: Profiles: Mike Pittilo|url=http://www.rgu.ac.uk/academicaffairs/committees/page.cfm?pge=29778|publisher=[[Robert Gordon University]]|accessdate=15 November 2009}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref> He then started work as an electron microscopist at [[Glasgow Royal Infirmary]], before taking up a post as a research assistant at the [[University of East London|North East London Polytechnic]], completing an [[Agricultural and Food Research Council|Agricultural Research Council]]-supported [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] on protozoan parasites of poultry in 1981.<ref name="RGU1"/><ref name="RGU2"/>

==Career==
After completing his doctorate, Pittilo worked as a postdoctoral research assistant at [[University College London Medical School|Middlesex Hospital Medical School]]<ref name="RGU2"/> from 1981 to 1985, before moving to [[Kingston University]] (then Kingston Polytechnic). He began as a lecturer, rising to become a senior lecturer and then reader, being appointed professor of biomedical sciences and head of the department of life sciences in 1992,<ref name="RGU1"/> and foundation dean of the university's shared faculty of health and social care sciences with [[St George's, University of London|St George's]], [[University of London]], in 1995,<ref name="RGU1"/> taking on additional responsibilities for multiprofessional education in 1996 and taught postgraduate courses in 1999.<ref name="RGU2"/> In 2001, Pittilo was appointed pro [[Chancellor (education)#Vice-chancellor|vice-chancellor]] of the University of Hertfordshire, a post he held until being appointed principal of the Robert Gordon University in 2005.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/education/principal-s-sudden-death-a-great-loss-to-higher-learning-1-790981|title=Principal's sudden death 'a great loss to higher learning'|work=[[The Scotsman]]|date=16 February 2010|accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref>

<ref>{{cite web|title=Pittilo appointed|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/pittilo-appointed/194472.article|work=[[The Times]]|date=4 March 2005|accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref> He was chairman of the Regulatory Working Groups for Herbal Medicine and Acupuncture at the [[Department of Health (United Kingdom)|Department of Health]] from 2002 to 2003, returning to the position in 2006.<ref name=ehtpa/>

==Personal life==
Pittilo married Carol Blow in 1987. He was a member of the [[Royal Society of Medicine]] and the Royal Northern and University Club, Aberdeen. He died on 16 February 2010.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/north_east/8518085.stm | work=BBC News | title=University principal dies aged 55|date=16 February 2010|access-date=15 November 2018}}</ref>
